tool.name: MMseqs2
tool.install: local, Homebrew bottle (arm64_tahoe); no sequence left this machine

algorithm.cluster_mode: 0 (Set-Cover greedy, MMseqs2 default), run as cascaded clustering
algorithm.note: Cascaded clustering can admit members that do not themselves meet the criteria against the representative; --cluster-reassign 1 reassigns them. -s 7.5 is the sensitive setting, chosen because 30% identity is remote and the default -s 4.0 would under-recall distant pairs. The SAME settings are used at all three identity thresholds so the three results are comparable.

sequence_identity_definition.meaning: identity counted over the ALIGNED length (identical aligned residue pairs / alignment length), not over the full or shorter sequence

coverage_requirement.meaning: BIDIRECTIONAL: the alignment must cover at least 80% of the query AND at least 80% of the target

input.population: ALL P1-P4 development proteins; E1/E2/E3 exclusion flags carried as columns, NOT applied
input.sequences: original full-length DeepLoc sequences, NOT ESM-truncated at 1022
input.nonstandard_residues: U(59) X(18) B(1) across 22 proteins, written verbatim; MMseqs2 maps unknown codes to X at scoring time; no substitution, no drop
input.isoforms: 268 isoform accessions resolved by their own accession; canonical never substituted

interpretation_limits: These are OPERATIONAL sequence-similarity clusters. They are not verified protein families and they are not proof of evolutionary independence.

Bidirectional 80% coverage requires global-ish similarity. It will MISS shared domains, partial homology, multi-domain proteins that share one domain, and homologous regions inside proteins of very different length. Two proteins in different clusters may still be substantially related.

Set-Cover clustering is greedy and representative-based. Membership is transitive through the representative, so a cluster is not guaranteed to be a clique: two members may be less similar to each other than each is to the representative.
Cluster counts are threshold- and coverage-dependent artifacts of this configuration, not intrinsic properties of the cohort.
Absence of a shared cluster is NOT evidence of absence of sequence similarity.
